title: t7: priority-max over 4 symbols in a 2-layer, 2-head transformer
label: partial: function verified by agreement, circuit localisation not verified
behavior: BOS + 4 tokens from 6 symbols (ti, ri, pu, bo, so, pa); the model outputs one symbol at the last position.
summary: The model outputs the highest-priority symbol present in the input under the fixed order pa > bo > pu > ri > ti > so, independent of position. A 4-line predict() matches the model on 200/200 held-out inputs twice (V0001 seed 2, V0002 seed 3). Mechanistically, layer-1 heads 1.0 and 1.1 attend from the last position to the winning symbol and mlp1 turns what they move into the answer logits; layer-0 heads pre-process the per-position representations that layer 1 moves (V-composition), and mlp0 is also required. All six components (4 heads, 2 MLPs) showed a causal effect, so I could not identify any component that plays no part. The circuit is therefore the whole model, which the lab cannot distinguish from a null on sufficiency (V0001: not-verified). The one pre-declared smaller circuit (dropping the weakest head, 0.0) kept 96.5% accuracy but only 0.682 of the logit difference, under the 0.7 threshold (V0002: not-verified). All numbers are from local-full (full precision).
pseudocode:
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    rank = {pa(7): 5, bo(5): 4, pu(4): 3, ri(3): 2, ti(2): 1, so(6): 0}
    return max(tokens[1:], key=rank)   # highest-priority symbol present

# mechanism (as far as measured)
# L0: heads 0.0/0.1 (+ mlp0) enrich each position's representation; no direct logit effect
# L1: heads 1.0/1.1 at the last position attend to the position of the highest-priority symbol and copy its (L0-enriched) value
# mlp1: converts the moved value into the output logits

claims.text: The model computes max under the order pa > bo > pu > ri > ti > so: predict() agrees with the model on 200/200 held-out inputs in two separate seeds; the model's own behaviour is confident (accuracy 1.0, mean logit diff 32).

Layer-1 heads 1.0 and 1.1 attend from the last position to the winning symbol wherever it is (0.83 and 0.92 for winner pu at position 3; 0.85 and 0.96 for winner pa at position 2 in the exploratory run), and jointly mean-ablating them leaves 0.17 of the logit difference.

Layer-0 heads 0.0 and 0.1 are needed (joint mean ablation leaves 0.27) but write almost nothing directly to the logits (0.004, 0.006); their main route is through the values of the layer-1 heads (0.18, 0.23), not their queries (0.02, 0.04, exploratory) or keys (0.03, 0.03).

Layer-1 heads have only a small direct effect on the logits (about 0.10 each) while mean-ablating mlp1 leaves 0.29 of the logit difference: the answer is finalised by mlp1. mlp0 is also necessary (0.23 left when ablated).
No single head carries the behaviour (largest single-head denoising effect 0.46; all four between 0.30 and 0.46), and no head or MLP was found to be inert.

Circuit localisation is not verified. Whole model as circuit: thresholds met but sufficiency has no null (V0001). Circuit without head 0.0: ablating it breaks the behaviour (fraction -0.03, accuracy 0.24) and it beats the null controls, but alone it retains 0.682 of the logit difference (accuracy 0.965), below the 0.7 threshold (V0002).

limitations: Circuit status is not-verified: the only circuit that meets the thresholds is the whole model, which has no sufficiency null.

The task statement says some components play no part; at head/MLP granularity I found none. Head 0.0 is the weakest (model keeps 96.5% accuracy without it) but it still carries 30% of the patching effect, so I do not call it inert.
Ablation and patching effects are logit differences against the corrupt prompt's answer; per-component accuracy was only seen in the two verification runs.
The path-patching primitive rejected mlp0 as a sender, so the mlp0 -> layer-1 and layer-1 -> mlp1 edges are inferred from ablations and direct-effect sizes, not measured as paths.
How layer-1 attention picks the winner (what is in the keys) and what exactly the layer-0 heads add to the values was not resolved.
The single-symbol output 'so' (all four inputs so) never appeared in the sampled data; the rule predicts 'so' there but this is untested.
One prediction was refuted (N0020: I expected no V-composition from layer 0 to layer 1; observed 0.23).
open_questions: What do heads 0.0/0.1 write at the source positions that makes the layer-1 values useful: a partial max, or a re-encoding of the token?
Is the priority order encoded in the layer-1 key/query weights directly on the token embeddings?
Would a finer-grained decomposition (per position, or neurons within the MLPs) reveal the inert parts the task statement mentions?
overall_status: partial / not verified · partial: function verified by agreement, circuit localisation not verified

refuted_predictions.hypothesis: Layer-0 heads influence the layer-1 heads little through their values as well (as with queries, E0011): the layer-1 heads read the winning token mainly from the embedding/mlp0 stream at the source position, not from layer-0 attention output.

prediction.statement: the larger of the two layer-0 -> layer-1 value path effects is at most 0.1
